title: Docs deep-link UX + UTM conventions for Console guided onboarding checklist
creator: Tessa Morgan
description:
Goal
Align Design + PM + Docs on a consistent, privacy-safe way for Redwood Console to deep-link users from the guided onboarding checklist into the docs site, while:
- attributing doc visits back to checklist steps (UTM conventions)
- ensuring links remain stable across docs IA changes (versioned/canonical URLs + redirects)
- providing predictable “back to Console” navigation patterns

Context
Phase 1 checklist lives in Console behind a feature flag. Most steps include a “Learn more” CTA to docs. We need link conventions now to avoid: broken links after IA changes, inconsistent analytics attribution, and confusing back navigation.

Out of scope
- Dedicated/Private onboarding deep links
- full SSO/SAML onboarding flows
- replatforming docs analytics (this ticket defines conventions only)

Deliverable
A short, written spec (below) that PM/Eng/Docs can implement consistently, plus example URLs and copy/UX guidance for opening behavior and back-navigation.
spec_body:
Proposed conventions (v1)

1) URL format + canonical routing
- Console must link to a canonical, version-stable docs URL (no release-numbered paths in Console).
- Docs team owns redirects from legacy paths to canonical.
- Canonical docs URLs should follow:
  - https://docs.redwoodinference.com/hosted-api/<topic-slug>
  - https://docs.redwoodinference.com/sdks/<language>/<topic-slug>
  - https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/<topic-slug>
- Avoid linking to nav-only pages that frequently move (e.g., landing pages) unless the checklist step is intentionally “overview”. Prefer the most task-oriented page.

2) UTM tagging (privacy-safe)
We will attribute traffic from checklist → docs using UTMs. Requirements:
- No org IDs, user IDs, email, project IDs, API keys, request IDs, or any dynamic identifiers.
- Only coarse attribution: entry point + checklist step slug + surface.
- Keep parameters consistent and allowlist-based.

UTM parameters (required)
- utm_source=console
- utm_medium=onboarding
- utm_campaign=guided_onboarding_checklist

UTM parameters (optional)
- utm_content=<step_slug>
  - example: utm_content=first_request
  - step_slug must be a static string from an allowlist (defined in checklist config)
- utm_term=<surface>
  - use for placement granularity when needed
  - allowed values: checklist_sidebar | checklist_card | empty_state | banner

Do not add additional custom query params in v1.

Examples
- First request step → docs:
  https://docs.redwoodinference.com/hosted-api/quickstart-first-request?utm_source=console&utm_medium=onboarding&utm_campaign=guided_onboarding_checklist&utm_content=first_request&utm_term=checklist_sidebar
- Rate limits / 429 guidance step → docs:
  https://docs.redwoodinference.com/hosted-api/rate-limits-and-quotas?utm_source=console&utm_medium=onboarding&utm_campaign=guided_onboarding_checklist&utm_content=rate_limits&utm_term=checklist_sidebar

3) Opening behavior (UX)
Default behavior for checklist “Learn more” links:
- Open in a new tab (target=_blank), because users typically need to reference docs while keeping Console state (checklist progress, keys page, usage dashboard) available.
- Include an external-link indicator in the UI + accessible label (e.g., aria-label: “Learn more about streaming (opens in a new tab)”).
- If a link is required to complete a step in the same flow (rare), PM must explicitly request a same-tab exception.

4) Back-navigation patterns
We will NOT rely on browser back as the only path back to Console.

Docs-side pattern (preferred)
- Docs pages that are heavily used by checklist steps should include a lightweight “Back to Console” link near the top of the article.
- The “Back to Console” link should point to a stable Console route (not step-specific state in v1):
  - https://console.redwoodinference.com/onboarding
  - or a relevant stable page when contextually correct (e.g., API keys page): https://console.redwoodinference.com/settings/api-keys
- Do not attempt to pre-select a step or include step completion triggers via query params.

Console-side pattern
- In Console, the checklist step row should retain a “Docs” deep-link even after completion (so users can revisit guidance without hunting in docs nav).

5) Versioning strategy + maintenance
- Console should link only to canonical docs URLs. If a page is renamed/moved, Docs team provides a redirect.
- Checklist config should store URLs as canonical strings (no per-release paths).
- Each URL used in the checklist must be validated in staging during release QA (simple 200 check + redirect check).

6) Measurement note
UTMs enable aggregate attribution in docs analytics. Console telemetry should separately measure “docs_link_clicked” per step (Console-side event) so we can correlate checklist engagement even if docs analytics are delayed or blocked.

7) Known constraints / future iteration ideas (not for v1)
- “return_to=” param from docs back to Console is intentionally deferred (risk: open redirect, security review overhead, and long-tail URL handling). Revisit if we see significant back-navigation confusion.
- If docs move to localized paths in the future, keep canonical stable in English and redirect by Accept-Language.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Agreement from PM (Marissa/Nikhil) and Docs (Elliot) on UTM parameter set and the explicit prohibition on dynamic identifiers.
2) Agreement that checklist deep links open in a new tab by default and include accessibility copy.
3) A short allowlist of step slugs for utm_content is defined (at least for Phase 1 steps).
4) A “Back to Console” pattern is agreed upon (docs-side link to stable Console route) and does not require passing user/org state.
5) Engineering has enough specificity to implement without further design clarification.
open_questions: Which Console route should the docs “Back to Console” link use as the single default: /onboarding vs /projects/<id>/onboarding? (v1 proposal: stable /onboarding; PM to confirm.)
Do we want utm_term values beyond the four listed, or keep tight until analytics requests expansion?
Should “opens in new tab” be included in visible text or only in accessible label + icon tooltip?
activity_log: 2026-01-23 — Kenji Nakamura: Drafted v1 conventions after reviewing checklist wireframes and docs IA draft. Proposed UTMs + canonical URL requirement.
2026-01-27 — Marissa Cole: PM feedback: +1 new tab default; requested we keep UTMs minimal and avoid anything that could be interpreted as user tracking.
2026-01-28 — Elliot Price: Docs feedback: canonical URL approach OK; docs can add redirects. Requested a stable list of deep-linked pages for QA.
2026-02-03 — Dylan Brooks: Engineering note: prefers no return_to param in v1 (open redirect risk). Suggested docs-side static “Back to Console” link instead.
2026-02-06 — Tessa Morgan: Design review: add explicit accessibility guidance for external links; approved spec with minor copy tweaks.
2026-02-12 — Kenji Nakamura: Marked Done; sent final conventions to PM/Docs and linked ENG-23123 for implementation.
comments: Marissa Cole (2026-01-27): Please keep this compatible with the privacy review posture: no user/org identifiers in query params. UTMs are fine if static/allowlisted.
Elliot Price (2026-01-28): We can support redirects from old docs paths. Please give us a concrete list of canonical URLs per checklist step so we can ensure stability and add redirect tests.
Dylan Brooks (2026-02-03): +1 avoid return_to for now. If we add it later, we’ll need an allowlist and security signoff. Static docs-side back link is simplest.
Nikhil Sharma (2026-02-05): Make sure the utm_content slug matches the step IDs we’ll use in Console telemetry so we can compare click-through vs completion.
